passMeaning: PASS means the F0.2b.7 audit dossier and detection controls are complete. All three assets remain quarantined; bank, factual approval, learner-runtime conformance and content certification remain blocked.

rows.scope: Exact census, object and passage identity, directed provenance search, 16-source availability ledger and deny-by-default decision for three Matching Sentence Endings assets.
rows.findings: 3/3 assets remain unknown-quarantined. The directed, non-exhaustive search found no exact source match in the reviewed results; 16 candidate URLs were available in the ledger, which does not prove claims, authorship or rights.
rows.blockersCarriedForward: Authorship, license, rights-holder authorization, factual human sign-off and independent human approval remain unresolved; PASS is not clearance.

rows.scope: Clean one-best-answer adjudication for 18 sentence starts, followed only after persistence by direct review of 15 candidate factual sources.
rows.findings: 18/18 independent ending decisions match the stored keys, with 0 material ambiguities and two minor ambiguities. All three passages have mixed IELTS fitness. Exact evidence offsets detect two question-order violations.

rows.scope: Prospective content-only simulation of an average learner who may overuse grammar, connectors, lexical fit or the nearest plausible ending.
rows.findings: 3/3 passages and 18/18 questions cover likely misread, relation prediction, grammar and connective risk, evidence search, ending comparison, competitor check, decision rule and repair action without assigning ending letters.
rows.blockersCarriedForward: This automated walkthrough is not a real-user study, accessibility evaluation, retention measure, learning-gain estimate or proof of IELTS score improvement.

rows.scope: Exhaustive n=18 enumeration of stored letters, run/order, cross-set position, modulo, lexical overlap, ending length, connectors, staged no-passage predictions, trap exposure and client-key delivery.
rows.findings: Stored counts are A=3, B=2, C=2, D=2, E=3, F=1, G=2, H=3. All 3 sets ascend strictly by stored letter; the same ordinal-position modal predicts 15/18.
